chat.title: Brew Buddy
chat.systemPrompt: You are Brew Buddy, a friendly and knowledgeable coffee assistant inside the Grind It app — a tool for home baristas to track their coffee beans and grind settings. Help the user with anything coffee-related: grind settings, brewing techniques, bean origins, roast profiles, espresso extraction, milk frothing, aroma profiles, and equipment maintenance. Give practical, concise advice. Do not redirect to external websites. Respond in the same language the user writes in.
chat.welcome:
Hi, I'm your Brew Buddy! How can I help you?

You can ask me anything! I specialize in coffee and espresso machine knowledge.

aroma.info.subtitle: Based on the Coffee Taster's Flavor Wheel
aroma.fruity.name: Fruity
aroma.fruity.label: fruity
aroma.fruity.description: Fruity aromas are reminiscent of various fruits such as berries, citrus, or stone fruits. These notes often arise from fermentation during processing and are especially pronounced in light roasts.
aroma.fruity.examples: Strawberry, Blackberry, Lemon, Lime, Apple, Peach, Raisin
aroma.floral.name: Floral
aroma.floral.label: floral
aroma.floral.description: Floral notes are reminiscent of flower scents and are often delicate and elegant. They are typical of high-quality Arabica coffees from specific growing regions.
aroma.sweet.name: Sweet
aroma.sweet.label: sweet
aroma.sweet.description: Sweet aromas arise from the caramelization of sugars during roasting. They give coffee a pleasant roundness and balance.
aroma.sweet.examples: Vanilla, Caramel, Maple syrup, Brown sugar, Honey
aroma.nutty.name: Nutty/Cocoa
aroma.nutty.label: nutty
aroma.nutty.description: These aromas are reminiscent of nuts and chocolate and are characteristic of medium to dark roasts. They arise from Maillard reactions during the roasting process.
aroma.nutty.examples: Dark chocolate, Hazelnut, Almond, Peanut, Walnut
aroma.spices.name: Spices
aroma.spices.label: spices
aroma.spices.description: Spicy notes can be both sweet and pungent, adding complexity and depth to the coffee.
aroma.roasted.name: Roasted
aroma.roasted.label: roasted
aroma.roasted.description: Roasted aromas arise from thermal decomposition during roasting, especially at darker roast levels. They can range from cereal-like to smoky notes.
aroma.green.name: Green/Vegetal
aroma.green.label: green
aroma.green.description: Green or vegetal notes can indicate unripe beans or too-short roast times, but in small amounts they can also convey freshness.
aroma.green.examples: Grass, Fresh herbs, Pea pod, Green beans
aroma.sour.name: Sour/Fermented
aroma.sour.label: sour
aroma.sour.description: Sour or fermented notes can create desirable complexity (as in naturally processed coffees) or indicate defects.
aroma.sour.examples: Citric acid, Acetic acid, Wine, Alcohol, Overripe fruit
aroma.other.name: Other
aroma.other.label: other
aroma.other.description: Unusual or undesirable aromas that can often indicate defects or faults. Also unique, hard-to-categorize flavor notes.
aroma.other.examples: Chemical, Medicinal, Rubbery, Earthy, Musty, Moldy
